title: From the Editor — Brannock Stayed
settingText: The road returning toward the Last Drop under late-afternoon glare. In the middle distance, a rough painted human figure is visible on an exterior wall but not readable in detail. The place feels familiar and changed at the same time.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 6. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: If you want to know whether a story can grow without anyone feeding it, go back to where it started.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Last Drop should be simple.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A half-heard name. A familiar face. A bad day turned into a better story after the witnesses had time to improve it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No preacher.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No investigator.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No experiment.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Just people.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Brandon left the Last Drop behind.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Brannock did not.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now they’re going back to see what stayed.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: The Road Back
summary: The trio deliberately backtracks toward the Last Drop to examine the one identity event known to predate Raina and Samuel.

panelPlan.text: The rig travels against its recent direction, making the return feel intentional rather than incidental.
Eva reviews the competing explanations: ordinary rumor growth, later Samuel contamination, or some other source.
Jessie points out that the Last Drop is useful precisely because they know how the first mistake happened.
Brandon is less interested in theory than whether Tomas survived and whether Marcus still controls the town.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: If Samuel never touched the first Brannock story, this is our cleanest case.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Cleanest is generous. We know where the first mistake came from.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I want to know whether Tomas is still alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is also useful information.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It is useful to Tomas.

title: The Mural
summary: Before the trio reaches the porch, they see a crude mural of a black-coated Brannock cutting a rope. The story has acquired a public body while Brandon was away.

panelPlan.text: The Last Drop comes into view. More people occupy the porch than before, and Marcus's former enforcers no longer control the entrance.
On the exterior wall is a rough hand-painted figure in a dark coat cutting a hanging rope, larger and broader than Brandon.
Eva stops talking mid-thought because the image answers a question she had not thought to ask.
Brandon studies the mural without amusement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They painted him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: They painted somebody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That is not an improvement.

title: A Different Porch
summary: The Last Drop's social geography has changed. People who once deferred to Marcus now use the porch and saloon without checking where his men are standing.

panelPlan.text: The trio crosses the same porch where Marcus's people once owned the best shade. Now workers, older locals and children occupy it casually.
A former enforcer carries a sack through the side door without receiving special attention.
Jessie notices the change before anyone explains it.
Several people recognize Brandon, but reactions vary: curiosity, gratitude, confusion and one cheerful toast to Brannock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Marcus lost the porch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That sounds small.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It isn't if everybody used to ask his permission to sit there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Brannock came back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Brandon did.

title: Tomas Standing
summary: Tomas appears alive, working and visibly recovering. He recognizes Brandon by his real name, establishing immediately that accurate memory and the Brannock legend now coexist.

panelPlan.text: Inside the saloon, Tomas carries a tray with some stiffness; rope scars remain visible above his collar.
He sees Brandon and smiles with uncomplicated recognition.
He calls him Brandon Mack loudly enough for nearby tables to hear.
Brandon's relief at seeing Tomas alive briefly overrides his discomfort with the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Brandon Mack. You came back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You look better standing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: It feels better too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You remember his real name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: He told us twice.

title: Marcus Left
summary: Tomas explains that Marcus was not defeated in a showdown. He left three days later after people stopped obeying him and his public authority failed to recover.

panelPlan.text: At a side table, Tomas describes the days after Brandon left.
Workers ignored one of Marcus's demands. A shopkeeper refused credit to his men. Two families moved their chairs onto the porch.
Marcus threatened consequences, but the audience no longer behaved like his threat was inevitable.
He packed and left before anyone had to fight him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: What happened to Marcus?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: He stayed three days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Then he realized people were waiting to see what he would do instead of doing what he said.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Attention shifted.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: So did the town.

title: What People Say Happened
summary: The saloon's popular version bears only loose resemblance to events: Brannock returned, cut down Marcus's victim, broke his power and disappeared before Marcus could answer.

panelPlan.text: At one table, a local retells the back-lot confrontation to visitors who were not there.
The story gives Brandon a deliberate entrance, a speech he never made and a clean political motive.
Eva quietly compares the retelling to what she witnessed.
Brandon refuses to correct every sentence because doing so would keep him at the center of the room all day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Brannock walked around back because he heard Marcus was hanging a man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He went around because he heard noise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Then he cut Tomas down in front of everybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That part happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: And told Marcus the town was finished with him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That part did not.

title: The Chain
summary: Tomas helps Eva reconstruct how the original story spread after the trio left: scarred patron to bartender, bartender to workers, workers to families and travelers.

panelPlan.text: Eva draws a simple sequence in her notebook while Tomas names who told whom.
The first retellings occurred before anyone from outside arrived.
Each step added interpretation: why Brandon intervened, whether he threatened Marcus and what Brannock supposedly wanted.
Jessie points out that no single reteller invented the final legend.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: The scarred man told the bartender before you were out of sight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then the bartender told the mill crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: The mill crew improved it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: And everybody remembers the version they received, not the version that started it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Nobody needed a Samuel.

title: Two Dead Brothers
summary: Eva samples contradictory Brannock biographies and finds the legend now contains details that cannot all be true, including a dead brother that multiplies between versions.

panelPlan.text: Eva moves between tables asking people what they know about Brannock without confirming Brandon's identity.
One person says Brannock returned because Marcus killed his brother. Another says Marcus killed two brothers. A third says the brothers died somewhere else entirely.
Tomas watches the contradictions with dry amusement.
Brandon asks Eva to stop before somebody gives him a wife and children.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Marcus killed Brannock's brother years ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second Local
dialogueInline.text: Brothers. There were two.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: By supper the first day, he had one. By morning he had two.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Please stop collecting relatives for me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I am documenting the damage.

title: Not Theirs
summary: Raina and Samuel arrive later and confirm the chronology. Samuel never visited the Last Drop before Brandon; Raina heard the Brannock story only after it had already traveled.

panelPlan.text: Raina and Samuel enter the saloon without trying to disguise why they came.
Eva puts Tomas's timeline beside Raina's earliest Brannock note.
Raina's date is clearly later than the original incident and early local retellings.
Samuel says he had never heard of the Last Drop before Raina brought him the story.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did either of you touch this before Brandon arrived?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I had never been here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Brannock is why I started looking for Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then the control case is actually clean.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Clean enough to ruin my first explanation.

title: The Man on the Wall
summary: Eva studies the Brannock mural as evidence of how memory hardens into an image. Brandon sees a version of himself the town can use without him.

panelPlan.text: Outside, the mural fills most of the wall: broad-shouldered black-coated Brannock cutting a rope under an exaggerated red sun.
Eva compares details: hair too short, coat too dramatic, knife too large, posture more heroic than Brandon's actual intervention.
Jessie watches Brandon's face and notices he is not merely embarrassed.
Tomas joins them and explains local painters worked from several people's memories.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The coat is wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Several things are wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: It isn't meant to be you exactly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That part is successful.

title: Put My Face On Him
summary: Brandon finally articulates why the mural bothers him. The problem is not that Brannock is admired; it is that a useful invented person has been given Brandon's face and can now authorize things Brandon never chose.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks whether Brandon would dislike the mural less if Brannock were depicted as a villain.
Brandon says the moral direction is secondary to the ownership problem.
Jessie understands that praise can erase him as effectively as accusation when both depend on an imposed identity.
A passerby touches the painted rope-cutting hand for luck, unintentionally proving the point.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Does it bother you more because people admire him?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: They made up somebody else and put my face on him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then people can ask Brannock to approve things Brandon never agreed to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Exactly.

title: What the Mural Means Here
summary: Tomas explains why locals keep the mural despite knowing it is inaccurate: it gives the community a shared image for the day Marcus stopped feeling inevitable.

panelPlan.text: Tomas stands beside the mural rather than defending its likeness.
He points toward the porch and back lot, explaining that people use the image to remember their own change in behavior.
Brandon suggests painting the porch instead. Tomas says people remember people more easily than furniture.
Eva sees that the false identity now serves a community purpose independent of Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: It is the day Marcus lost the porch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then paint the porch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: People don't remember porches.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: They remember Brannock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: They remember what they did after he left.

title: A Committee
summary: Several locals approach Brandon with a practical problem: they have formed a committee to prevent another Marcus, but they want Brannock's signature to make the arrangement feel legitimate.

panelPlan.text: Inside the saloon, three locals bring Brandon a handwritten agreement defining rotating responsibilities for security, disputes and common stores.
The agreement itself is practical and locally authored.
At the bottom, they have left a prominent space for BRANNOCK'S endorsement.
Eva sees why they think the signature would protect the committee if Marcus returns.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: We wrote the rules ourselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then why is there a space for me?

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: If Marcus comes back, we show him Brannock backs us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It would probably help.

title: Sign It Brannock
summary: The locals make the request explicit. Brandon refuses to sign under Brannock's name because doing so would transform the accidental legend into authority he personally endorsed.

panelPlan.text: A local offers Brandon the pen and points to the blank endorsement line.
Brandon asks what name they expect him to use.
They answer Brannock because Brandon Mack carries no local reputation.
Brandon puts the pen down without touching the paper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Sign it Brannock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then I'm not signing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Marcus will laugh at our names.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. At least he'll know who is actually standing there.

title: The Next Brannock
summary: Brandon shows the committee the structural problem with borrowing Brannock's authority: once the invented identity can legitimize policy, anyone who controls the story can claim to speak for him later.

panelPlan.text: Brandon asks what happens if another traveler arrives claiming to carry Brannock's orders.
Eva points out that the town already believed one false Brannock from appearance and story momentum.
Jessie adds that Marcus could manufacture his own Brannock story just as easily once the name has official force.
The committee members begin looking at the blank endorsement line differently.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: What happens when somebody else's Brannock signs the opposite order?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You already know how easy the first mistake was.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: A legend is a poor lock. Anybody with the story can try the key.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Then what are we supposed to show Marcus?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Each other.

title: Hear the Rules
summary: Brandon refuses the endorsement but agrees to listen to the committee's actual plan, separating rejection of borrowed authority from indifference to what the town is building.

panelPlan.text: The committee assumes Brandon's refusal means he is leaving the conversation.
Instead, he asks them to explain how rotating watch duty works and who can remove someone abusing it.
Tomas joins and points out a weakness: the storekeeper and watch leader should not be the same person.
Eva realizes Brandon is willing to discuss the substance as Brandon, not bless it as Brannock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I won't sign as Brannock. I can still hear what you wrote.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: You think the rotation is wrong?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I think Tomas has a point about putting the keys and the watch in one hand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: I have several points now that nobody is hanging me.

title: Their Names
summary: The committee removes the Brannock endorsement line and replaces it with the names of the actual residents agreeing to the plan.

panelPlan.text: A local strikes through the blank Brannock line.
One by one, residents sign their own names beneath the agreement.
Some sign confidently; others hesitate because public ownership feels riskier than mythical backing.
Tomas signs slowly, still recovering strength in one hand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: He may laugh at us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Marcus laughed before. We still stopped listening.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That part matters more than the paper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The paper helps you remember who agreed.

title: If Marcus Returns
summary: The town considers the possibility that Marcus returns. The answer is deliberately unheroic: no Brannock, no promised showdown, just enough people refusing to restore the old arrangement.

panelPlan.text: A younger resident asks what happens if Marcus returns with armed help.
The committee's first instinct is to look at Brandon; he deliberately looks at Tomas instead.
Tomas says they call everyone to the porch and decide together whether Marcus enters.
Brandon nods without turning that nod into endorsement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Young Local
dialogueInline.text: What if Marcus comes back with men?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Then he finds more people on the porch than he left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That answer belongs to you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: No Brannock required.

title: Thank You, Brandon
summary: At the door, Tomas thanks Brandon by his real name in front of the room for cutting the rope. The gratitude is specific to an act Brandon actually performed, not the Brannock legend.

panelPlan.text: The trio prepares to leave. Raina and Samuel stand nearby but do not turn the moment into analysis.
Tomas calls Brandon back by his full name.
He thanks him specifically for cutting the rope and staying long enough to make sure he was breathing.
Nearby patrons hear the real name without correcting Tomas.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Brandon Mack, I never thanked you properly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You survived. That was enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: It is enough for you. I still wanted to say it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then I heard you.

title: Two Names in One Room
summary: The Last Drop now holds Brandon and Brannock simultaneously. Some locals know Brandon's name and use it; others keep Brannock as a folk figure. The legend no longer depends on believing the two are literally the same man.

panelPlan.text: One patron raises a cup to Brannock while another asks Brandon whether the road south is passable.
Tomas answers a newcomer who asks whether Brandon is Brannock by saying Brandon is Brandon and the mural is Brannock.
Raina sees that correcting the factual identity has not erased the social identity.
Brandon accepts a wrapped meal from the bartender under his own name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Newcomer
dialogueInline.text: So he isn't Brannock?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: He is Brandon. Brannock is what people call the story.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: They know your name and kept the other one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Tomas didn't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Some of us don't need Brannock anymore.

title: Raina's Control Case
summary: On the road, Raina concedes that the first Brannock case demonstrates how much pattern can emerge from ordinary social processes without her intervention.

panelPlan.text: The five travel the same road for a short stretch, Raina and Samuel alongside rather than ahead.
Raina summarizes only what the Last Drop actually proved: initial mishearing, resemblance, old local legend and uncontrolled retelling.
Eva points out that this does not explain Merritt or the blue-room phrase.
Raina agrees by leaving those items uncrossed in her notes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Brannock does not require a hidden organizer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It requires people, time and a story they want.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: That is enough more often than investigators like to admit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It still doesn't explain everything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: No. It explains one case properly instead of all cases badly.

title: Brandon Mack
summary: Eva asks Brandon how it feels to know the Last Drop can distinguish him from Brannock and still keep the legend. Brandon admits it bothers him, but the trio continues toward a place where nobody is waiting for any name at all.

panelPlan.text: Raina and Samuel peel off toward another nearby route, leaving the trio alone in the rig again.
Eva asks whether the coexistence of Brandon and Brannock makes the mural easier to tolerate.
Brandon says the town knowing better matters more than the paint.
Final wide panel: the road ahead opens toward greener patches around Rowan Hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Does it still bother you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It does.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Less than before?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Tomas knows who thanked him. That helps.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Maybe the next place won't call you anything interesting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I would consider that a gift.

title: Next: NO NAMES TODAY
settingText: A peaceful road toward Rowan Hold at morning, fields and family structures beyond, with no threatening silhouettes. An old black Sunforge rib sits in the yard with a goat on it; the page should feel almost comically uneventful.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The first story grew without help.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The town knows Brandon’s real name and keeps Brannock anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So the road offers a new experiment:

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: a place with no old name waiting,

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: no planted story,

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: no one demanding Brandon become somebody else.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: What happens when nothing happens?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: NO NAMES TODAY
